key_insight: Jev, a decision language model, showed competitive agreement with physician ratings and LLM judges while costing less and running faster than frontier judges.
clinical_relevance: Lower-cost, faster judging could make clinical AI output evaluation more scalable, but does not establish clinical safety or patient benefit.
method: Compared Jev’s structured judgments with frontier and open-weight LLM judges across four use cases.
Measured agreement with physician ratings on pediatric answers and HealthBench criteria.
Compared judgments with an LLM jury on MedHELM and a reference judge on HealthBench Professional.
evidence_signal: On 118 pediatric answers, Jev achieved Gwet’s AC2 of 0.50; it matched the HealthBench Professional reference judge on 91% of criteria, while frontier judges cost 73–294 times more and took 7–57 times longer.
watch_item: Agreement with an LLM jury or reference judge is not independent evidence of clinical correctness; broader physician validation remains important.
paper_title: Decision language models as affordable and rapid alternatives to LLM judges of clinical generative AI
